conclusion: No output-quality or resource-efficiency advantage established in this pilot. Optional availability produced zero lookups; required lookup cost more and did not improve rubric scores.
isolation: Fresh Docker network=none, readonly root, new tmpfs HOME; no private data/history/config/credentials or other candidates mounted. Read-only public retrieval via per-run socket; base route denied. Signed-in model credentials remained in trusted host broker.
token_definition: Input includes cached tokens; total=input+output. Cache is provider prefix reuse, not prior user memory. Usage covers participant agent loop, including tool steps; not protocol preparation, embedding compute, grader or total project cost.
latency_boundary: Descriptive sum of per-task monotonic container times, no shared-host workload isolation; an interrupted grading overlap affected late primary runs. One run per arm/task, not a stable speed estimate.
expertise_boundary: Two task-specific rubric items from one blind model grader. Not an independent human or domain-expert assessment.
other_limits: Four synthetic tasks selected from current catalog coverage; near-ceiling results.
Required-lookup condition was added after observing 0/4 optional lookups, after three coding grades were exposed; exploratory on same tasks, no fresh holdout.
The no-resource baseline does not include general web search, flat-document RAG, or a competitive memory product.
The coding tasks returned no matching context. Design and career retrieved one full method each.
No graph traversal was requested by the agents. This does not establish graph-specific value.
No real users, field outcomes, long-term preference transfer or billed dollar savings measured.
